note: B-A's row is REPORTED, not gated, for this run: --under-coload declares that the harness shares its host with unrelated concurrent work, and B-A is the daemon-observed hook_controlled estimate (recvTS - reqTS + tail allowance) whose reqTS is stamped inside the spawned hook process, so under co-load the interval contains the child's scheduling wait — a cross-process latency with no CPU-time analogue to gate instead (on windows-latest, one commit: bench-gate, harness alone on its runner, measured this row's p99 at 3.072ms; two whole-tree test-job runs minutes apart measured 11.264ms then 18.432ms against the 15ms limit, while the spawn floor's p50 went 12.954 → 24.431 / 23.143ms). note: B-B's p99 CANNOT be certified and its gate is failed on that ground: 522 of the 2064 planned samples never reached the daemon's histogram and are counted as over-budget samples, which puts the full population's nearest-rank p99 at rank 2044 of 2064 — inside the un-delivered block, since only 1542 samples were observed. The p99 field reports the DELIVERED set's own p99 for diagnosis only; it is a lower bound on the real one, never the gated number

note: B-B's row is REPORTED, not gated, for this run: --under-coload declares that the harness shares its host with unrelated concurrent work, and B-B times the daemon's own ingest.Accept in full — a region that has carried three fsyncs (the WAL Sync, the lease journal's Sync and the seal) since f6a8691 made the delivery path durable, so co-load moves it like any other wall-clock cost (the last full parallel pass measured this row's p99 at 14.3 / 28.7 / 53.2ms against the 15ms limit, while three runs of the same build inside an attested quiet window measured 20.480 / 12.288 / 20.480ms). There is no CPU-time analogue to gate instead: B-B has no child process, so the user+system time of a spawned child cannot be read for it; obs.ProcessCPU is a cumulative whole-process counter summed over every thread, quantised to Windows's 15.625ms scheduler tick (internal/obs/cpu_windows.go), so a single-request bracket against a limit in the low tens of milliseconds reads exact zero, which that file requires be

treated as a FAILED measurement; and what inflates this row is fsync — blocked time that costs no CPU at all. The 15ms limit is still enforced on B-B by every run that does NOT pass --under-coload — bench-gate, nightly bench-deep, ci.yml's timing job (which runs test/integration's hot-path test alone by name) and its test-e2e job, where X-11 runs alone — and the co-load-immune structural gates T9, T10 and T14 (one sync per batch, check-then-append order, zero releases before the seal; internal/daemon's delivery group-commit tests) run in every lane regardless. This is ADR 0010's fallback branch applied to a row its enumeration misclassified, per SP20-D1 design section 7.6's Q3; internal/obs/budgets.go still marks B-B Gated, and only this RUN reports it

note: B-E's wall-clock row is REPORTED, not gated, for this run: --under-coload declares that the harness shares its host with unrelated concurrent work, and a wall-clock sample taken under co-load measures the host's spare capacity rather than the checkpoint (bench-gate measured this same row at 67.2ms on windows-latest in isolation and the whole-tree job at 4302ms on the same runner class minutes later, product unchanged). The 2000ms limit is still enforced on that wall-clock row by every run that does NOT pass --under-coload — bench-gate and nightly — and the B-E_cpu row below enforces the same 2000ms limit on these children's own CPU time, which co-load does not move; see budgetIDBECPU (report.go)

note: hook_ack_rtt is REPORTED, never gated: it is the client-side ACK round trip of 64 in-process observe.tool deliveries, each with a fresh nonce and a real lease, timed through the same ipc.Client a hook uses. Design §7.5 sizes the ACK deadline from it as AckDeadlineMs = L0IngestMs + ceil(slack99), where slack99 = p99(hook_ack_rtt) - p99(B-B) over this same run. The timed samples are preceded by 2 DISCARDED warm-up requests on the same session: without them sample #0 paid a session-registry insertion and a WAL segment create on top of the round trip, and at 64 samples with nearest-rank percentiles p99 IS the maximum sample, so that one sample became the number the deadline was sized from. Its traffic IS real hot-path traffic, so all 66 requests do reach the daemon's l0_ingest and hook_controlled histograms — but this run reads both of those for the gated B-A and B-B rows BEFORE any of the tranche is sent, warm-ups included, so none of it is inside either gated population, and the B-B this row

is differenced against contains none of its own deliveries. They are reconciled rather than ignored: a second status read after the tranche counts every one of them, warm-ups included, into the delivery ledger, so a deferral of this tranche's own cannot pass unnoticed. The in-process traffic that does sit inside the gated populations is the warm-up's, disclosed with its own computed proportion. A p99 over 64 samples is still that set's own top sample, which is why §7.5 takes the maximum across three runs rather than trusting one

note: daemon-observed hook_controlled_observed (recvTS-reqTS, strict lower bound, no hotPathTailAllowance): p50=2.048ms p99=7.168ms n=1542 — informational cross-check against the gated B-A row above, which adds the tail allowance

note: B-A's gated n=2064 includes 64 in-process warm-up observe.tool requests (Send-time TS, not a spawned process's main() entry) alongside 2000 real hook spawns from the B-A/B-D loop — the warm-up hot-path tranche (warmHotTranche=64, a small, fixed constant) is 3.1% of the gated population for this run; see B-A_spawn_estimate for the wall-clock diagnostic derived purely from real spawns
